links.outcome: Readability of chatbot and AAPOS website amblyopia responses versus recommended reading level
links.effect: Readability analyses (FRE, FKGL, CLI) showed AAPOS website and chatbot responses were more challenging than the recommended level; ChatGPT-3.5 hardest to read.
links.quote: Three readability analyses showed that Bard had the highest mean score, followed by the AAPOS website, Bing Chat, and ChatGPT-3.5, and these scores were more challenging than the recommended level.

links.outcome: Understandability and actionability (PEMAT) of chatbot patient education responses versus website
links.effect: PEMAT-U: website 81.5%, Bard 77.6%, ChatGPT-3.5 76.1%, Bing Chat 71.5% (P<.05); PEMAT-A: website 74.6%, Bard 69.2%, ChatGPT-3.5 67.8%, Bing Chat 64.8% (P<.05).
links.quote: The AAPOS website and chatbots, especially Chat-GPT, provided difficult-to-read data for patient education regarding amblyopia.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the readability, understandability, actionability, and appropriateness of three LLM chatbots for amblyopia patient education against official web resources, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
